cancer_indication: Estrogen-receptor–positive (ER+) / hormone-receptor–positive (HR+) breast cancer (adjuvant and metastatic), ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), and risk-reduction in high-risk women.
moa: Tamoxifen is a non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator that competitively antagonizes estrogen receptor-α (ESR1) in breast tissue, blocking estrogen-driven transcription of proliferative genes and promoting growth arrest and apoptosis in ER+ disease. It is a prodrug metabolized mainly by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4/5 into active metabolites (4-hydroxytamoxifen and (Z)-endoxifen) with higher affinity for ERα that largely drive clinical efficacy. Long-term exposure can reshape signaling networks, with endocrine-resistant states characterized by activation of bypass survival pathways (e.g., PI3K/AKT/mTOR, ERBB/EGFR) and programs such as Hedgehog, EMT, and NF-κB; tamoxifen can also act as an agonist at GPER1 in some contexts.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.description: Estrogen-regulated transcriptional program reflecting ER-driven gene expression in estrogen-responsive cells.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_EARLY.interpretation: Captures ER dependence and luminal differentiation programs that underpin hormone-driven proliferation in ER+ breast cancer.

REACTOME_ESTROGEN_DEPENDENT_NUCLEAR_EVEN.description: Nuclear ESR1-dependent transcriptional events downstream of estrogen signaling, including regulation of gene expression programs linked to proliferation and survival.
REACTOME_ESTROGEN_DEPENDENT_NUCLEAR_EVEN.interpretation: Represents the core ESR1-linked transcriptional machinery that drives hormone-dependent growth in ER+ tumors.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Genes regulated by E2F transcription factors involved in G1/S transition, DNA replication, and proliferation.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: Reflects proliferative output downstream of ER signaling and cell-cycle control that influences tumor growth dynamics in ER+ disease.

KEGG_P53_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: p53-mediated stress response controlling cell-cycle arrest, DNA damage responses, and apoptosis.
KEGG_P53_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Links tumor suppressor control of growth arrest and apoptosis to treatment response pathways in ER+ breast cancer.

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Transcriptional response to IFN-γ, including immune activation and antigen-presentation-associated genes.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: Represents immune-active microenvironment features reported as associated with endocrine outcomes in ER+/HER2– breast cancer.

HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.description: PI3K/AKT/mTOR survival and growth signaling controlling proliferation, metabolism, and anti-apoptotic programs.
HALLMARK_PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING.interpretation: A major growth/survival axis that provides ER-bypass signaling in endocrine-treated ER+ breast cancer and shapes therapeutic response states.

KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: ERBB receptor tyrosine kinase signaling (e.g., EGFR/ERBB2) and downstream MAPK/PI3K pathways.
KEGG_ERBB_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: Growth-factor signaling cross-talks with ER programs and modulates proliferation and survival circuitry in ER+ and HR+/HER2+ breast cancer.

HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.description: Transcriptional program associated with activation of RAS/MAPK signaling outputs.
HALLMARK_KRAS_SIGNALING_UP.interpretation: Represents proliferative signaling programs that can support growth and pathway rewiring in endocrine-treated breast cancer.

KEGG_HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.description: Hedgehog pathway signaling regulating GLI-mediated transcription and developmental programs.
KEGG_HEDGEHOG_SIGNALING_PATHWAY.interpretation: A developmental signaling axis described as involved in endocrine therapy resistance programs in ER+ breast cancer.

HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.description: EMT-associated gene program involving loss of epithelial traits and gain of mesenchymal features linked to invasion and plasticity.
HALLMARK_EPITHELIAL_MESENCHYMAL_TRANSITI.interpretation: Represents cellular-state changes associated with invasiveness and endocrine-resistant phenotypes in breast cancer models.

HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB.description: TNF-induced NF-κB pathway activation driving inflammatory and pro-survival transcriptional responses.
HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB.interpretation: Inflammatory survival signaling described in tamoxifen-resistant contexts in ER+ breast cancer models.

KEGG_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.description: Homologous recombination DNA repair pathway for double-strand break repair involving core HR machinery.
KEGG_HOMOLOGOUS_RECOMBINATION.interpretation: DNA repair capacity and related DDR adaptations are described as altered in endocrine-resistant contexts in the provided evidence.

KEGG_GAP_JUNCTION.description: Gap junction-mediated intercellular communication involving connexins and cell–cell coupling pathways.
KEGG_GAP_JUNCTION.interpretation: Cell–cell adhesion/communication features (including Connexin-43) are described as linked to epithelial state and endocrine response phenotypes.

KEGG_DRUG_METABOLISM_CYTOCHROME_P450.description: Cytochrome P450-mediated drug metabolism processes affecting biotransformation and clearance of xenobiotics.
KEGG_DRUG_METABOLISM_CYTOCHROME_P450.interpretation: Relevant to tamoxifen as a prodrug requiring CYP-mediated bioactivation to active metabolites that drive ER antagonism in breast cancer.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High ESR1/ER dependence and higher estrogen-response scores are described as associated with better endocrine benefit in ER+/HER2– breast cancer.
Adequate CYP2D6 function is described as important for forming endoxifen; lower endoxifen levels in poor metabolizers or with CYP2D6 inhibition are associated with worse clinical outcomes.
Higher Connexin-43 (GJA1) expression and related junctional pathways are described as correlating with tamoxifen sensitivity and opposing EMT-like resistance states.
Luminal differentiation gene signatures including GATA3 are described as correlating with endocrine responsiveness in ER+ breast cancer.
Luminal differentiation gene signatures including FOXA1 are described as correlating with endocrine responsiveness in ER+ breast cancer.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation via mechanisms including PIK3CA mutation is described as a major endocrine (tamoxifen) resistance route in ER+ breast cancer contexts.
Upregulation/amplification of HER2 (ERBB2) is described as promoting endocrine resistance by driving downstream MAPK and PI3K signaling and reducing ER dependence.
EGFR upregulation is described as contributing to tamoxifen-resistant growth via downstream MAPK/PI3K signaling in ER+ breast cancer models.
IGF1R upregulation is described as part of growth factor pathway activation that drives ligand-independent proliferation and endocrine resistance circuitry.
FGFR1 upregulation is described as contributing to growth-factor-driven bypass signaling (MAPK/PI3K) in tamoxifen-resistant contexts.
In tamoxifen-resistant cells, PI3K/AKT activity is described as upregulating BARD1/BRCA1 and increasing HR repair capacity, contributing to resistance.
In tamoxifen-resistant cells, increased BRCA1-associated HR repair capacity is described as part of a resistance-associated adaptation.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Reduced Connexin-43 (GJA1) expression is described as linked to EMT-associated tamoxifen resistance via signaling feedback loops.
Decreased CYP2D6 activity (poor metabolizer phenotype or potent inhibitors) is described as lowering endoxifen levels and reducing tamoxifen efficacy.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2– (Luminal A/B): Primary population for tamoxifen benefit in adjuvant and metastatic settings; strong evidence from many randomized trials and meta-analyses. Sensitivity pathways noted include high estrogen response, luminal differentiation, intact p53, low PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and epithelial phenotype; resistance pathways noted include PI3K/AKT/mTOR upregulation, Hedgehog activation, EMT, NF-κB, and ESR1 alterations.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2+ / HR+: Tamoxifen is used with chemotherapy and HER2-targeted therapy; HER2 overexpression and downstream PI3K/MAPK activation predispose to resistance.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.TNBC / ER–: No role for tamoxifen; lack of ER expression confers intrinsic resistance and tamoxifen is not recommended.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-mutated / HRD+: Direct tamoxifen sensitivity data are limited; where ER+ and BRCA2-mutated, tumors can still benefit, but DDR pathway modulation of tamoxifen sensitivity is described as indirect.
